title: AI Coding Toolkit Implementation Dataflow — Nodes and Containers
description: impl-dataflow is shorthand for implementation dataflow. This JSON models proposed designs or implemented behavior using a flat array of typed dataflow nodes and class/module containers. Functions and mutable state belong to containers; static data may optionally belong to a container. Membership is distinct from class composition. Dataflow relationships connect nodes, and composition relationships connect class containers. Diff hunks provide code-review evidence.
$comment: Schema version 18. Semantic validation must check that node and container IDs are unique across both arrays, container names are unique, function names are unique within each source file and owner, other owned node names are unique within each owner and subtype, and unowned node names are unique among unowned nodes. Resolve every containerId and endpoint ID explicitly, and verify that endpoint types match referenced entities. Diff-hunk IDs must be unique, every reference must resolve, and every diff hunk must be referenced by a node, container, or relationship. Validate derived counts against nodes and relationships. These cross-entry checks cannot be enforced by this static JSON Schema alone.

schemaVersion.description: Version of the Implementation Dataflow schema used by this document.

stage.description: The development stage represented by this dataflow: proposed implementation during high-level design or implemented behavior during code review.

diffHunks.description: Exact unified diff hunks referenced by nodes, containers, and relationships during code review. Every hunk must be referenced at least once.

changedClassCount.description: Derived number of class containers owning at least one function, state-variable, or static-data node whose changeType is added, modified, or deleted. Container status is derived solely from owned nodes, not from composition relationships or diff-hunk references.

changedFunctionCount.description: Derived number of function nodes whose changeType is added, modified, or deleted, across class and module containers.

changedComponentCount.description: Derived number of added, modified, or deleted UI, system input/output, and external dependency components.

changedDataflowRelationshipCount.description: Derived number of added, modified, or deleted dataflow relationships, including state reads and writes.

nodes.description: One entry per represented dataflow entity. Node IDs are unique across nodes and containers. Function names are unique within their source file and owner; other owned node names are unique within their owner and subtype, so names may repeat across files or owners. Names of unowned nodes are unique among unowned nodes. Use explicit IDs for references; never infer identity from a name.

containers.description: Class and module containers for function, state-variable, and optionally owned static-data nodes. Membership is recorded only by each owned node's containerId. Container names are unique among containers; IDs are unique across nodes and containers. Derive container status from all owned nodes, including hidden nodes: new when all are added, unchanged when all are unchanged or there are no owned nodes, deleted when all are deleted, and changed for mixed statuses or modified children. Do not store an independent changeType. Optional diff-hunk references provide evidence for the container independently of its derived status.

relationships.description: Direct data transfers, state accesses, and class composition. Preserve intermediate participants. Dataflows express dependencies and data movement, not execution order. Container membership is not a relationship.

file.description: Repository-relative path to the changed file.

patch.description: Exact unified diff hunk, including the @@ header.

diffHunkIds.description: References to relevant diff hunks, permitted only during code review. Required for actual changed nodes and relationships; omitted for unchanged entries and missing-from-cr markers. Containers may reference relevant hunks independently of their derived member status.

changeType.description: How an entity or relationship differs from the existing architecture. Use added for a new entry, modified for a changed declaration, responsibility, contract, or relationship, deleted for a removed entry, and unchanged for an existing entry reused without such a change. Participation or a new connection alone does not modify an endpoint.

codeReviewEvidence.description: Actual changed nodes and relationships require supporting diff hunks; unchanged entries must omit diffHunkIds. Missing-from-cr function markers carry expected change types and omit evidence. Containers retain optional evidence independently of member status.

sourceFile.description: Repository-relative intended final source-file path using forward slashes. For a deleted entity, use its last existing path.

renamedFrom.description: Original identity of an entity intentionally renamed or moved.

functionRenamedFrom.description: Original function identity. Provide containerName when moving the function from an unrelated class or module.

nodeBase.description: Shared properties of every dataflow node. Subtypes define ownership and connection semantics.

id.description: Explicit entity ID, unique across nodes and containers. References use this ID rather than the name.

name.description: Human-readable name. Owned node names are unique within their owner and subtype; unowned node names are unique among unowned nodes.

description.description: What this node is or represents, including a concrete URL, file path, storage key, or other identifier when relevant.

initialization.description: True when the node represents one-time initialization code and/or code that does not participate in a User Journey defined in the High Level Requirements. This includes, but is not limited to, constructor code, callback plumbing, object/dependency graph construction, etc. False otherwise.

node.description: A function, boundary component, static-data source, or mutable state variable. Each subtype shares nodeBase properties and preserves its own connection rules.

ownedNode.description: A node owned by exactly one class or module container. This containerId is the sole membership record; it does not express composition.

containerId.description: ID of the owning class or module container. The referenced container must exist.

function.description: An implementation function owned by a class or module. Functions can exchange data with other functions and boundary nodes, read static data, and read or write mutable state.

subtype.description: Code-review marker for a function change expected by the HLD but missing from the CR graph; not an implemented function.

hld-change-mismatch.description: Optional function-level mismatch flag assigned by annotate-hld-function-coverage.mjs after comparison with the HLD.

hldChangeType.description: The matching HLD function's planned change type, copied onto an actual code-review function by annotate-hld-function-coverage.mjs; null means the function is absent from the HLD. Missing-from-cr markers already carry the HLD expectation in changeType.

boundaryNode.description: A UI surface, system input or output, or external dependency. Represent implementation handlers and adapters as function nodes instead.

uiComponent.description: A UI surface that receives user input or presents output. May send and receive data. Has no container owner.

systemInput.description: Data supplied to this system by another system or workflow. May only be the source of a dataflow. Has no container owner.

systemOutput.description: A final result sent to another system or workflow. May only be the target of a dataflow. Has no container owner.

externalDependency.description: An external service, file, datastore, or other I/O endpoint used by the implementation. May send and receive data. Has no container owner.

staticData.description: Fixed data that is significant to the design or patch. Some examples would be configuration files or static data files used for object initialization . Contant varibles in the code may be included as static data if they are truely significant to the design or patch, but this is usually not the case. If this is the case, group together contants in the same class/module under one staticData node. May only send data to functions. May optionally belong to a class or module through containerId. External files and storage are external-dependency nodes.

containerId.description: Optional ID of the owning class or module container. The referenced container must exist.

stateVariable.description: Mutable state owned by a class or module: mutable instance fields for classes, or mutable module-scoped variables for modules. Include changed declarations and unchanged state referenced by dataflows. Exclude local variables, explicitly read-only values, fields initialized at declaration or construction but never written afterward, and fields used only as references to owned child objects. Constructor assignment is initialization rather than a state update. Runtime writes alone do not make an existing variable modified. May only exchange data with functions: state-to-function means a read; function-to-state means a write.

container.description: A class or module grouping function, state-variable, and optionally owned static-data nodes through their containerId. Both types may own any combination of these node types. Derive container status from all owned nodes, including hidden nodes: new when all are added, unchanged when all are unchanged or there are no owned nodes, deleted when all are deleted, and changed for mixed statuses or modified children. Do not store changeType. Container diffHunkIds remain optional during code review, including when owned nodes are unchanged. Class composition is separate from membership.

id.description: Explicit entity ID, unique across nodes and containers.

oneOf.description: An implementation class containing member functions, mutable instance state, and static data.
A named implementation unit containing functions, mutable module state, and static data. May be a language-level module, namespace, package, or source file.

generatedBy.description: Marks a container created solely to own missing-from-cr function nodes, allowing the annotation script to remove it when no longer needed.

nodeEndpoint.description: Typed reference to a node by explicit ID. Semantic validation must resolve nodeId and confirm that type matches the referenced node.

transferSourceEndpoint.description: A function, UI component, system input, or external dependency sending data. System outputs cannot send data.

transferTargetEndpoint.description: A function, UI component, system output, or external dependency receiving data. System inputs cannot receive data.

functionEndpoint.description: A reference to a function node.

staticDataEndpoint.description: A reference to fixed data. Valid only as the source of a read by a function.

stateVariableEndpoint.description: A reference to mutable state. Valid only when the other endpoint is a function.

classContainerEndpoint.description: Typed reference to a class container by explicit ID. Semantic validation must resolve containerId and confirm that the container is a class.

oneOf.description: A direct transfer between function or boundary endpoints, a static-data read by a function, or a mutable state read/write by a function. System inputs may only send and system outputs may only receive. Record request and response paths separately.

One class owns instances of another class. Connect class containers, not nodes. This is distinct from a function or state variable belonging to a container. A field used only to reference an owned child object is represented by composition rather than as a state-variable node.

relationship.description: A direct dataflow between typed node endpoints or a composition between typed class-container endpoints.

from.description: Explicit typed source reference, constrained by relationship type.

to.description: Explicit typed target reference, constrained by relationship type.

transferType.description: Required only for function-to-function dataflows. arguments passes data from caller to callee through call arguments; return passes return data from callee to caller. Record the two directions separately, even when the visualizer draws them as one edge.

dataDescription.description: What data this relationship transfers, reads, or modifies.

oneOf.description: Direct data transfer between functions and boundary nodes, respecting system-input and system-output directionality.
Static-data read: fixed data is the source and a function is the target. Static data cannot receive writes.
State read: a state variable is the source and a function is the target.
State write: a function is the source and a state variable is the target.
